transcript.content: Hello, it's nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, it's nice to meet you too. Um... I came in because I just seem to worry about everything lately. I mean, literally everything. My clients, the real estate market, my family, money... even just whether moving into my new condo was the right decision. It just feels like it's out of proportion to what's actually going on, you know? It's just constant.
How long have you been feeling this constantly worried?
I'd say it's been going on for about a year and two months now. It pretty much started right after I sold my longtime house and made the move into the condo.
Is your worry mainly about the move and your new condo, or does it also involve many unrelated areas of your life?

Well, like I mentioned a minute ago, it really involves everything. The condo move is just one part of it. It spills over into totally unrelated areas of my life—my clients, the housing market, my family, my finances. It just feels like I'm worrying about all of it, and it's just way out of proportion to what's actually happening in any of those areas.
Since these worries began, have you been feeling depressed most days?

No, I wouldn't say I've been feeling depressed. I mean, I don't really feel sad or down most days. It's really just the constant stressing and worrying about things that's bothering me, but no, not depressed.
When you try to stop or control the worrying, how difficult is that for you?

It's really difficult. I mean, even when I try to stop and tell myself, you know, 'Parin, this is not urgent,' it doesn't seem to help. One concern just leads right into another one, and before I even realize it, I've spent half an hour just replaying small details in my head that I really meant to let go of. It's just very hard to turn it off.
Since the worrying began, have you had difficulty sleeping?

Yes, I have. Most nights I actually get into bed at a reasonable hour, but my mind just keeps circling. I'll start thinking about condo fees, or tomorrow’s showings, or I'll worry about whether I missed a detail in a client's contract. It takes me a really long time to finally settle down, so when I do wake up in the morning, I just feel like I never fully rested.
Do you often feel restless or on edge?

No, I wouldn't say I feel restless. I mean, I can sit still at my desk or on the couch just fine without needing to pace around or anything. It's... it's really just my mind that feels like it's racing, not my body. So, no, I don't really get that keyed up or on-edge feeling.
Since the worrying began, have you often felt fatigued or unusually tired during the day?

No, not really. I mean, I know I said I don't always feel fully rested when I wake up, but I wouldn't say I feel unusually tired or fatigued during the day. I still have the energy to get through my work and do what I need to do. It's just the mornings that are a bit slow.
Since the worrying began, have you often had trouble concentrating or found your mind going blank?

Yes, I have noticed some trouble with that. Especially at work. When I’m reviewing purchase agreements or inspection addendums, I’ll end up reading the same paragraph three or four times. A worry just pops into my head, and I completely lose the thread of what I was checking.
Since the worrying began, have you often experienced muscle tension, such as tightness or aching in your neck, shoulders, or other muscles?

Yes, I do. By the time the evening rolls around, my neck and shoulders feel really tight, almost like I've been bracing myself all day. I've also noticed that I'll catch myself clenching my jaw, especially when I'm driving between listings or just sitting at my desk working.
